integration_cautions: This is a reviewed-source expansion, not complete global or Americas coverage. Seven new records do not necessarily represent seven disjoint peoples.
Keep data/nations/overrides.json, verify/human.json, and all existing takedowns unchanged. The two Bhil named-person holds remain in force.

The historical merge.py has GENERATED fixed at 2026-10-08 and expects raw/verify/respect files beside its supplied --dir and tools/merge_overrides.json. Do not blindly regenerate the live registry from it; integrate into the durable import pipeline and retain actual per-fact receipts.

The Tonto Apache ITCA page still contains old 85-acre and pending-land-legislation statements. Those were not used. Its dated historical removal account was used alongside the later BIA account of trust acquisition.
The Ute Mountain Ute homepage gives conflicting chairman term lengths. No officeholder, term-length or current population claim was imported.
Chiricahua Apache Nation is kept as its own named self-identifying community. No federal-recognition status, exclusive treaty succession, or territorial jurisdiction claim is inferred.
The generic Ute record remains a peoples overview; only three government-name aliases and its misleading single-government official_url were removed. Its existing fact receipts were preserved.
Source matching is separate from an integrating reviewer checking the meaning of each paraphrase. The research sidecars explicitly identify their agent authorship.
Resource links are research recommendations here; adding this context file alone does not create links in the public UI.

public_notes.text: This entry follows this named community's own published account. It does not identify a single representative for all Chiricahua people or establish federal-recognition status.
This is a Ute peoples overview. The linked records describe distinct tribal governments; they are not aliases for one government or an exhaustive list of Ute-identifying communities.
This record describes the Fort Sill Apache Tribe. Related Chiricahua records describe distinct communities or governments; this page does not merge them or claim exclusive representation.
This record describes the Lipan Apache Tribe in Texas. Mescalero's own account also includes Lipan people. The linked records are not treated as one government.
The April 1, 2026 statement announced an intention to appeal. It is not a current docket record and does not establish an appeal filing or outcome.
The ITCA page also includes older land-base and pending-legislation statements. The dated historical facts here do not state the Tribe's current acreage or current legislative status.
